name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain = play/anim cinematic). Accurately reflects purpose: the per-character zoom-in + palette-fade intro animation played at the start of special-attack / summon / combat / ending cinematics. No Ghidra address residue in the name; no domain ID present.
purpose: Plays a 9-frame slide-in + palette-darkening fade-in 'character sweeps onto the screen' intro for one character inside a special-attack / summon / combat-hit cinematic backdrop, before the per-hit FIGANI frames run.
logic_summary: Branches on data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[char_unit_id].team. team!=0 (ally/player) -> TOP-HALF: for frame 8..0, clear workspace from bg_sprite, optionally (mode_flag==0) lay the static char sprite (char_sprite2), RLE-blit the name-banner backdrop (weapon_sprite) at (0xA4,0x9D) and the sliding overlay (char_sprite) at workspace+frame*10, push to VGA 0xA0000, ramp palette by frame*6 (max 8*6=0x30 down to 0); final settle RLE-blits the backdrop into bg_sprite at stride 0x140. team==0 (enemy) -> BOTTOM-HALF at workspace+0x140 origin with reversed slide (base - iter*10): optionally settle backdrop first, then per frame 8..0 clear region, blit sliding overlay, optional static layer, push to VGA, ramp palette by iter*6.
signature: void fd2_play_char_intro_zoom_anim(uint32 char_unit_id, uint32 mode_flag, uint32 char_sprite, uint32 char_sprite2, uint32 workspace, uint32 bg_sprite, uint32 weapon_sprite)

params.name: char_unit_id
params.semantics: Runtime-char array index; only its .team field is read to pick TOP-HALF (ally/player, team!=0) vs BOTTOM-HALF (enemy, team==0) display + slide direction. Every caller passes the unit being introduced (caster/attacker, or party member in the ch30 ending).
params.reason: Accurate; indexes runtime_char and selects display half via .team. No address residue.

params.name: mode_flag
params.semantics: 0 = also draw the static character-sprite layer (char_sprite2); nonzero = skip it (caller pre-composited the char into the backdrop, e.g. split-screen 1-on-1). Callers pass 0, 1, or the FIGANI split_screen_flag / (spell_id!=0x1C).
params.reason: Accurate gate name; matches all 6 call sites.

params.name: char_sprite
params.semantics: Sliding overlay sprite handle, blitted every frame at the moving offset (workspace+frame*10 top-half, base-iter*10 bottom-half).
params.reason: Accurate; this is the per-frame sliding sprite.

params.name: char_sprite2
params.semantics: Static character sprite handle, blitted at the fixed origin when mode_flag==0. Some callers pass 0 (no static layer) or the same handle as char_sprite.
params.reason: Accurate; this is the fixed (non-sliding) layer drawn only when mode_flag==0.

params.name: workspace
params.semantics: Composite work buffer base; the 0x280-stride slide region. Bottom-half path uses workspace+0x140 as the region origin. Callers pass the 0x1F400 work buffer.
params.reason: Accurate; the off-screen composite buffer (0x280 stride).

params.name: bg_sprite
params.semantics: Clear source (copied into the workspace region every frame, 0x140 stride) and the final-settle RLE destination. Callers pass the 64000-byte mode-13h backdrop scratch (dst).
params.reason: Accurate; clear source + settle destination at 0x140 stride.

params.name: weapon_sprite
params.semantics: RLE backdrop (name-banner) sprite blitted at (0xA4,0x9D). Despite the name it is NEVER a weapon: all 6 callers pass a TAI.DAT / FDSHAP.DAT name-banner / character-base sprite (verified: fd2_play_figani_char_intro_animation/fd2_play_full_combat_cinematic/fd2_execute_special_attack_skill/fd2_execute_summon_spell_cast/fd2_play_final_chapter_30_ending pass TAI.DAT, fd2_play_spell_cast_sequence passes FDSHAP.DAT[3]).
params.reason: Current name is misleading -- the value is never a weapon; it is the RLE name-banner / character-base backdrop. Sibling fn fd2_execute_combat_hit_cinematic already calls the identical TAI.DAT sprite param 'name_banner_sprite'. Rename recorded only; applied in Stage 2 (touches protos.h decls + all call sites).

returns.semantics: No return value; the effect is the on-screen zoom/fade animation pushed to the mode-13h framebuffer at 0xA0000 and the resulting palette state.

reads_globals: data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr (0x53A45) -- reads [char_unit_id].team to choose top/bottom-half display and slide direction
comment_original_issue: Two factual/wording defects in the existing block: (1) line stated fade ramps 'from 0x36 down to 0' but the loop counter runs 8..0 with step 6, so max = 8*6 = 0x30 (arithmetic error, corrected to 0x30 with the 8*6 derivation spelled out); (2) 'Positional args mirror the two callers in this file' was slightly stale -- the arg semantics are consistent across all 6 callers (reworded), and the weapon_sprite line was tightened to state it is never a weapon (RLE name-banner backdrop at (0xA4,0x9D)).

issues.title: Duplicate fd2_play_char_intro_zoom_anim prototype in protos.h with divergent param names
issues.description: protos.h declares fd2_play_char_intro_zoom_anim twice: line 190 (params caster_idx, mode_flag, caster_figani_a, target_figani0, workbuf2, workbuf1, tai_resource) and lines 524-527 (char_unit_id, mode_flag, char_sprite, char_sprite2, workspace, bg_sprite, weapon_sprite). Both have identical types (7x uint32, void) so it compiles, but the duplicate + divergent names are an inconsistency. Recommend removing the line-190 copy during Stage 2 (when the param rename to name_banner_sprite is also applied) so a single canonical declaration remains. Not modified this stage (declaration-level change reserved for Stage 2).

notes: Verified all 6 callers' call sites (decompiled fd2_execute_special_attack_skill, fd2_execute_summon_spell_cast, fd2_play_figani_char_intro_animation, fd2_play_full_combat_cinematic, fd2_play_spell_cast_sequence, fd2_play_final_chapter_30_ending) -- ABI param order matches the C signature exactly; Ghidra's decompiled local var names (char_idx/mode_flag/base_sprite) are a Ghidra naming artifact and do NOT reflect the true stack-slot semantics. Confirmed runtime_char.team field name in rebuild types.h:24 (uint8 @ +0x06, 0=enemy/1=npc/2=player) -- src comment's .team is correct; Ghidra plate's .bTeam is the Hungarian-prefixed Ghidra struct field for the same member (non-contradictory, plate left unchanged). Ghidra plate already accurate (correct 0x30 fade max, 'never a weapon' note) so left as-is per refine rule.
